NUM_RE allows 1-digit decimals which yields false precision (e.g., 88.1 formatted as 88.10 while a correct 88.17 exists in another pass). Guidance should recommend requiring exactly 2 decimal digits for monetary totals and only fall back to looser pattern if nothing found.

Multi-pass OCR section is present but not integrated with field extraction: no instruction to run extraction on each pass and vote / prefer higher-precision agreement; the batch pipeline uses only PSM 6 then multi_pass fallback as raw string concat, which actually hurts tier selection by duplicating candidates.

Two-line fallback only looks forward one line; no guidance for right-column amounts, backward look, or using image_to_data with bounding boxes to associate keyword line with the rightmost number on the same horizontal band.

Preprocessing guidance does not mandate upscaling for small/low-DPI receipts; evidence shows 2x upscale materially improves digit accuracy (e.g., 074 102.00 recovered, 064 88.17 recovered). Skill mentions upscaling only conditionally.
Null-handling rule exists in prose ('set to None, not empty string') but no code pattern enforces it when writing to pandas/openpyxl; evidence shows '' leaked into Excel for 078.

No explicit guidance that string-typed numeric fields written via pandas can be coerced to float or empty string; needs explicit recipe: use dtype=object, write None (not NaN/empty), and verify via load_workbook data_only read that cells are either str or empty (None), especially for amounts that must retain trailing zeros.

Missing checklist item: verify sheet name exactly matches required ('results'), only one sheet exists, column order and header casing match spec; current xlsx skill emphasizes formulas but not strict schema conformance for data-dump tasks.

Change NUM_RE guidance to prefer exactly 2 decimal digits for monetary totals: '\\d{1,3}(?:,\\d{3})+\\.\\d{2}|\\d+\\.\\d{2}'. Mandate multi-pass OCR as the default pipeline for receipts: run pytesseract on {raw, grayscale+autocontrast, 2x-upscale+grayscale+autocontrast} with PSM {6,4,11}, then run extract_total/extract_date on EACH output separately and vote. Add date disambiguation rule: parse date with ALL plausible patterns (DD/MM/YYYY, MM/DD/YYYY, YYYY/MM/DD, DD MMM YYYY). Prefer parse where day>12 to lock orientation. root_causes.description: Voting across OCR variants trusts noisy variants equally: a single corrupted upscaled read ('702.00','688.17','100.00','23.25') can override cleaner reads. Priority tier is applied per-variant before cross-variant consensus, so a lower-quality variant that happens to match a higher-priority keyword wins over higher-quality variants matching a lower tier.

Keyword fallback to the 'next non-empty line' is applied unconditionally when a tier-matched line has no number; it does not exclude lines that are clearly payment/change/visa/cash-received, so noise lines like 'Visa RM =688.17' become the chosen total.

Within a tier, the implementation prefers the LAST matching line, but for receipts with a rounded 'Total' line followed by a 'Grand Total' or final 'TOTAL:' line, cross-variant disagreement is resolved by frequency rather than by picking the lexically latest keyword occurrence or the strictly highest-priority keyword present in the cleanest variant.

Date parsing has no locale heuristic: when both '09/03/2018' and '08/09' style numbers appear nearby (e.g., time stamps, item codes), the parser can match the wrong triple and does not re-score candidates by proximity to 'Date' / 'DATE' tokens or by DD/MM/YYYY preference for Malaysian receipts.

The pipeline lacks a disciplined, bounded strategy: Skill guidance encourages multi-pass OCR but gives no explicit stopping rule, cross-variant arbitration rule, or sanity checks (e.g., total must be <= cash tendered + change, must appear in >=2 variants when possible). This leads the agent into open-ended tuning loops.
image-ocr Skill does not specify how to combine priority tiers with multi-pass OCR or how to reject payment-line fallbacks; agent re-invented a brittle voting scheme from scratch inside one run.

skill_defects.defect: Multi-pass OCR section recommends combining text from several variants but gives no deterministic arbitration rule for conflicting field values; no guidance to prefer the variant with the highest-priority keyword tier AND most repeated numeric value, nor to abstain when variants disagree with no majority.

Total-extraction rules do not restrict the two-line fallback: they allow falling through to any non-excluded next line, which lets payment lines (Visa/Cash/Card) masquerade as totals. Exclusions list is not expanded with payment keywords like VISA, MASTERCARD, PAYMENT, TENDER, RECEIVED.

Within-tier tie-breaking is under-specified. The skill should state: 'If multiple lines in the same priority tier match, prefer the one appearing LAST in reading order AND whose numeric value also appears on an immediately preceding/following summary line (sanity check), unless a stricter keyword (GRAND TOTAL, final TOTAL:) occurs later.'

Date extraction lacks a locality rule: it does not instruct to anchor the match to a 'Date' / 'DATE' / 'Tarikh' label when present, nor to prefer DD/MM/YYYY for receipts with 'RM' currency, nor to reject year/month/day triples that overlap with timestamps or invoice numbers.

No explicit iteration/complexity budget: the skill does not advise capping OCR variants (e.g., 2-3) and committing after a sanity-checked result, nor does it tell the agent to abstain (null) rather than keep searching once a confident candidate exists.

Quality self-check list omits concrete numeric sanity checks for receipts: total should not equal cash tendered or change; total should not be a payment-method amount; if a Rounding Adj line follows a provisional total, prefer the FINAL rounded TOTAL line.

xlsx guidance does not specifically remind that for OCR output pipelines the amount column must be written as string with trailing zeros preserved and that empty extractions must be written as empty cells (None), not as empty string ''. One prediction row shows total_amount='' which is a schema violation.

No cross-field consistency rule: when OCR confidence for either field is low, the skill should suggest returning null for that field rather than guessing, which would raise field_accuracy over joint accuracy for ambiguous receipts.

repair_recommendations.change: Add a 'Multi-pass Arbitration' subsection: run exactly 2-3 OCR variants (default, autocontrast grayscale PSM 6, optional 2x upscale PSM 6). For each variant compute (tier_index, value). Final choice: (a) pick the smallest tier_index observed across variants; (b) within that tier, pick the value with the highest multiplicity; (c) break ties by preferring the value that also appears somewhere in another variant's text (even outside a keyword line); (d) if no value repeats across variants AND tier_index > 1, return null rather than guess.

Expand EXCLUSIONS to also cover payment/tender lines: add 'VISA','MASTERCARD','DEBIT','CREDIT','PAYMENT','TENDER','TENDERED','RECEIVED','CARD','CASH RECEIVED','BALANCE','ROUNDING'. Specify that during the two-line fallback, the fallback line must still pass the exclusion filter; otherwise skip and continue to the next tier candidate instead of accepting it.

Formalize within-tier selection: 'If a tier matches multiple lines, scan the lines bottom-to-top; prefer the match whose numeric value equals or follows an earlier line with the same keyword (confirming a final rounded total). If a strictly higher-priority keyword (GRAND TOTAL / final TOTAL:) exists later in the document, prefer that over an earlier same-tier match.'

Rewrite the Date Extraction section to: (1) first search for lines containing 'DATE', 'TARIKH', 'INVOICE DATE', 'BILL DATE' and only parse date patterns on those lines or the next non-empty one; (2) default to DD/MM/YYYY for 2-digit-first patterns, YYYY-MM-DD when year is 4 digits first; (3) reject matches that are substrings of longer digit runs (invoice numbers, barcodes); (4) if multiple candidate dates disagree across OCR variants, pick the one that appears in >=2 variants; else null.

Add an explicit Budget & Stopping Rule: 'Do not run more than 3 OCR variants per image. After arbitration, do not retry OCR unless both fields are null. Prefer returning null for a field over spending additional turns tuning preprocessing.' This directly addresses iteration exhaustion.

Add Numeric Sanity Checks: (a) reject totals equal to CASH or CHANGE or payment-method amount on the same receipt; (b) if a 'Rounding Adj' line is present, prefer the TOTAL line that appears AFTER it; (c) reject totals whose integer part has >5 digits unless currency symbol confirms (filters OCR glitches like 702.00 vs 102.00 — require a corroborating same-value elsewhere in the text).

Clarify null-emission contract: 'When writing to tabular output, failed extractions MUST be Python None (empty cell), never empty string, never NaN text, never 0. total_amount MUST be a string formatted with f"{v:.2f}" or None.' Include a short code snippet showing object-dtype column and None preservation.

Add a short 'OCR output tables' note: emphasize using pandas with object dtype for monetary strings, writing None (not '') for missing values, and sorting rows lexicographically by filename. Reference image-ocr skill for formatting rules so pipelines stay consistent.

Add a 'Common Receipt Pitfalls' subsection listing concrete failure modes seen in practice: upscaling can corrupt digits ('102'→'702', '88'→'688'); payment lines mimic totals; rounding-adjusted totals differ from pre-rounding totals; dates often appear in DD/MM/YY near store footer. Provide one-sentence mitigation for each — these generalize beyond this specific run.

Recommend a lightweight self-consistency check function (pseudocode) that, given extracted (date, total) and the raw OCR text, verifies: total string appears verbatim in >=1 variant; date components appear on a labeled line; otherwise downgrades the field to null. Encourage calling it before writing the row.

observed_failures.issue: OCR misread '102.00' as '702.00' on the 'Total Amt Rounded' line; majority vote across OCR variants picks the misread value because two of three variants agreed on 702 while only one variant produced the correct 102.00 (which appeared multiple times in that variant on Subtotal/Total incl./Payment lines).

Picked the 'Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26' line but the receipt's final TOTAL after rounding adjustment is 23.25. Candidate selection preferred the 'Total ... GST' line over the final 'TOTAL:' line, likely because the final 'TOTAL:' line was treated differently or the inclusive-of-GST match ranked higher within the generic TOTAL tier.

Grand Total line was mangled across all OCR variants; two-line fallback was blocked by digits/exclusions and candidate voting at the best available tier produced a non-total value (observed intermediate predictions 100.00 and 20.00 before refinements). Final output empty indicates no safe candidate was selectable.

Date on receipt is 09/03/2018; prediction '2018-08-09' indicates month/day swap. Date parser likely matched DD/MM/YYYY but then also matched a different numeric triple (e.g., GST ID 000800589824 → '08/05/89' or similar) or interpreted '09/03/2018' with the wrong format when multiple candidates were present.

root_causes.summary: Keyword-priority selection is per-OCR-variant and uses majority vote across variants, with no cross-line corroboration
root_causes.detail: When OCR misreads a single digit on the final total line (e.g., 102→702), two of three variants can agree on the wrong value while the correct value is corroborated by Subtotal/Payment/Cash lines in another variant. Voting ignores this intra-receipt corroboration and picks the OCR-majority wrong value.

root_causes.summary: Ambiguity between 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' and the final rounded 'TOTAL:' line
root_causes.detail: Some receipts show an inclusive-of-GST total followed by a rounding adjustment and a final 'TOTAL:' value differing by a few cents. The generic TOTAL tier treats both as equal matches; without preferring the last (rounded) TOTAL after rounding adjustments, the wrong value is chosen.

root_causes.summary: Two-line fallback for keyword-only lines is too restrictive and/or exclusion set is incomplete for payment-adjacent lines
root_causes.detail: When the keyword line loses its number due to OCR, the fallback (take last number on next line) can pick up payment lines like 'Cash Received', 'Visa RM', or 'Mastercard'. Early iterations missed 'Cash Received'; conversely tightening fallback to only pure-keyword lines caused 078 to return null when the Grand Total line was mangled with stray characters but no valid digits.

root_causes.summary: Date extractor has no disambiguation when multiple date-like substrings exist
root_causes.detail: Receipts contain additional numeric strings (GST IDs, invoice numbers, phone numbers) that can match loose date patterns; without anchoring on 'Date:' labels or scoring by proximity to date keywords, the parser can pick a false positive and misinterpret DD/MM vs MM/DD.

root_causes.summary: No post-selection sanity check against subtotal + tax + rounding
root_causes.detail: The pipeline doesn't validate the chosen total against subtotal + GST/SST + rounding adjustment present on the same receipt, which would have caught the 702 vs 102 case and the 23.26 vs 23.25 case.

skill_defects.defect: Current candidate skill documents a priority-tier matcher and two-line fallback but does not mandate (a) cross-line corroboration via Subtotal/Payment/Cash agreement, (b) preference for the final rounded TOTAL after a 'Rounding Adj' line, (c) a sanity check that selected total ≈ subtotal + tax ± rounding, or (d) a robust fallback rule that distinguishes pure-keyword lines from garbled-number lines without silently returning payment amounts.

Exclusion list in the skill text enumerates CASH TENDERED but not CASH RECEIVED, CASH PAYMENT, VISA, MASTERCARD, DEBIT, CREDIT, CARD, PAID, TENDER, ROUNDING, ROUNDED (as a standalone label), AVERAGE / PAX, POINTS, CHANGE DUE — all of which have appeared as fallback traps on realistic receipts.

Date extraction section lacks guidance to prefer dates adjacent to 'Date', 'Tarikh', 'Invoice Date', 'Receipt Date', 'Bill Date' labels, and to reject date-like matches that overlap GST IDs, phone numbers, or invoice/transaction numbers. No DD/MM vs MM/DD disambiguation heuristic (e.g., first field >12 ⇒ DD/MM; year position; locale hint 'RM' ⇒ Malaysian DD/MM/YYYY).

Multi-pass OCR strategy does not specify a voting/arbitration policy that uses evidence from the same receipt (subtotal, payment, change) to break ties between OCR variants; defaults to simple frequency which is misleading when two variants share the same misread.

Skill does not describe a 'summary region' concept (lines after items, before footer) nor instruct to restrict keyword search to that region, which would reduce false matches on item descriptions containing 'TOTAL' or 'AMOUNT' as part of column headers.

Guidance confirms writing strings for total_amount but does not warn specifically about pandas inferring float on empty-mixed columns or openpyxl writing a numeric cell when a Python float sneaks in; a stronger rule to force dtype=object and format with f'{v:.2f}' before assignment is needed for this class of OCR-to-Excel task.

No explicit instruction that None/null fields must be written as truly empty cells (not the string 'None', not NaN rendered as text) and that the sheet must contain exactly the required columns in the required order with the required sheet name.

repair_recommendations.change: Expand the Receipt Field Extraction section to require a cross-line corroboration step: after selecting a candidate total T at the best available tier, count how many times T (or T within ±0.02) appears elsewhere in the OCR text as Subtotal, Total incl. GST, Payment, Cash, Rounded Total, Net Total, Amount Due. If an alternative tier-matched value T' has strictly more corroboration occurrences than T, prefer T'. Document this as the 'corroboration tiebreak' with pseudocode and worked example (102 vs 702 on a safety-pins receipt).

Add a rule: when both an 'inclusive of GST' total and a later 'TOTAL' / 'Total Rounded' / 'Net Total' / 'Grand Total' / 'Total After Rounding' appear, prefer the LATER rounded value. Formalize this by scanning top-to-bottom and, within the same priority tier, taking the last match that is on or after a line matching a rounding indicator (ROUND, ROUNDING, ROUNDED, ADJ, NET).

Rewrite the two-line fallback rule precisely: trigger ONLY when the keyword line contains no digits AND the next non-empty line is not a payment/change/tax/discount/points line. Provide an explicit extended exclusion regex covering CASH\s+(TENDERED|RECEIVED|PAYMENT|PAID)?, VISA, MASTER(CARD)?, DEBIT, CREDIT, CARD, TENDER(ED)?, PAID, CHANGE(\s+DUE)?, ROUNDING(\s+ADJ.*)?, POINTS, AVERAGE(\s*/\s*PAX)?, TAX, GST, SST, SUB\s*TOTAL, DISCOUNT, SAVINGS.

Add a 'summary region' heuristic: locate the first line after the item table (detected by a run of lines containing a trailing numeric with 2 decimals plus a quantity column) and restrict total-keyword search to that region through the footer. Fall back to full-text search only if no candidates are found.

Strengthen date extraction with: (1) prefer matches on lines containing DATE, TARIKH, INVOICE DATE, RECEIPT DATE, BILL DATE, PRINT DATE; (2) if multiple matches, score by proximity to such labels and recency to the TOTAL region; (3) disambiguate ambiguous NN/NN/NNNN: if first group >12 ⇒ DD/MM; if second group >12 ⇒ MM/DD; otherwise default to DD/MM/YYYY for RM-denominated receipts and document this locale default; (4) reject date substrings that overlap known non-date fields (GST ID, phone, invoice number) by requiring a word boundary and not being part of a longer digit run.

Add a sanity-check pass: if subtotal S and tax T are detectable, require that |chosen_total − (S + T + rounding_adj)| ≤ 0.05; otherwise demote the chosen candidate and retry with the next candidate. Document rounding_adj parsing (signed decimal near a ROUNDING/ADJ keyword).

Document the multi-pass voting policy explicitly: for each OCR variant, collect ALL (tier_idx, value) candidates; aggregate across variants; pick (min tier_idx, then max corroboration count, then max cross-variant frequency, then last-occurrence tiebreak). Include a worked example and a note that simple cross-variant majority is insufficient when two variants share the same OCR misread.

Normalize numeric parsing: strip currency prefixes RM, MYR, $, and trailing letters/codes (S, SR, SRM, SRS, C, A, T) before parsing; accept comma thousands separators; collapse spaced decimals ('86 17'→'86.17' when flanked by RM-style context) only under a conservative rule to avoid over-correction; and reject values with implausible magnitudes (e.g., >100000 or <0.01) unless corroborated.

Add explicit guidance that per-image failure must yield None for the failed field without raising, and that the output row must still be emitted; include a batch loop template that catches exceptions per file.

In the output-schema guidance for this family of tasks, require: single sheet named exactly as specified; columns in the exact order; sort rows by filename as strings; total_amount written as a Python str with exactly two decimals via f'{v:.2f}' and the column dtype forced to object before to_excel; date written as 'YYYY-MM-DD' string or None; None values written as truly empty cells (never 'None' or 'nan'); verify by reloading the workbook with openpyxl data_only=True and asserting the cell types and values match.
Add a short checklist: no extra sheets, no extra columns, no header renaming, no trailing blank rows; use pd.ExcelWriter with engine='openpyxl' and df.to_excel(..., index=False).

Current logic takes the first/priority keyword match and ignores downstream rounded totals.

The current DATE_PATTERNS list in the candidate skill tries '%d-%m-%Y' before '%m-%d-%Y' but does not use locale/receipt-origin hints and does not sanity-check against plausible day/month ranges beyond year. root_causes.description: Total-extraction keyword priority not implemented correctly. On receipts using 'Net Total' (tier 4) with a stray number like a table ref or OCR noise, the extractor seems to pick the last/largest number anywhere rather than the number on the matched keyword line. Current skill text describes priority tiers but code pattern in draft takes first-matching tier and 'last number on that line' — on OCR'd 074 the Net Total line may lose its number or be split, and fallback picked an unrelated number (e.g., '702' from OCR garbage or merged digits).

Skill does not treat 'Rounding Adj' / 'Total After Rounding' / final 'TOTAL:' as highest-priority when a pre-rounding 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' line precedes it. Priority tiers lack rules preferring the post-rounding final TOTAL on receipts with explicit rounding adjustments.

When primary keyword search fails (e.g., 'Grand Total' line present but OCR line order/segmentation breaks keyword match), the pipeline writes empty string instead of None, and does not attempt the documented multi-pass OCR fallback nor a last-resort 'largest decimal number near TOTAL region' heuristic. Also distinction between None and '' not enforced when writing xlsx (empty cell vs empty string).

Date parser's pattern ordering is ambiguous: `(\d{1,2})[-/](\d{1,2})[-/](\d{4})` with fmt '%d-%m-%Y' is correct for DD/MM/YYYY, but on 034.jpg ('09/03/2018') the agent produced 2018-08-09, suggesting either a different code path matched '%m-%d-%Y' or an OCR misread of '03' as '08'. Skill lacks explicit guidance that Malaysian receipts in this dataset are DD/MM/YYYY and should NEVER be parsed as MM/DD/YYYY, plus no sanity re-check against OCR text.

No validation step comparing extracted total against plausible numeric range on the receipt (e.g., consistency with Subtotal + GST, or presence of currency prefix 'RM'). A simple sanity check (final total ≥ subtotal, within 2x of max line amount) would catch 702.00 vs 189.75.

skill_defects.defect: Total extraction logic underspecified for rounding-adjusted receipts: no rule to prefer 'Total After Rounding' / final 'TOTAL' line over earlier 'Total Inclusive of GST'. 'GRAND TOTAL' is top priority but code does not explicitly add 'TOTAL AFTER ROUNDING' or 'NET TOTAL' with higher priority than generic 'TOTAL'.

Null-vs-empty-string handling not enforced in the pipeline/output writer. The skill shows `rows.append({'total_amount': None})` but does not warn that pandas may coerce None to '' or NaN when dtype is object; needs explicit guidance to write None and verify empty cell in xlsx.

Date disambiguation guidance missing for ambiguous DD/MM vs MM/DD. The DATE_PATTERNS list has `%d-%m-%Y` before `%m-%d-%Y` but no explicit rule or regional heuristic documented. On Malaysian/SG receipts, DD/MM/YYYY is standard; skill should state this preference and show a validation (month ≤ 12, day ≤ 31, and if ambiguous prefer DD/MM).

No fallback 'largest plausible monetary value near keyword' or multi-pass retry when keyword match yields no number; receipt 078 produced empty rather than retrying with alternative PSM/preprocessing or scanning for 'Grand Total' variations with whitespace/OCR noise.
No sanity-check / cross-validation: comparing extracted total to subtotal+tax, or verifying it is the largest 'total-like' value, would catch picks like 702.00 on a 189.75 receipt.

Guidance for writing a column that must preserve string-with-2-decimals and allow None/empty-cell is absent. Should document pattern: build DataFrame with object dtype, assign None (not '', not NaN) for missing, and verify in opened workbook that empty cells are truly empty.

Priority keyword list ordering not sufficiently explicit about 'TOTAL (Inclusive of GST)' vs 'Total After Rounding'/'TOTAL:' precedence; also lacks explicit mention of 'Rounded Total', 'Total Rounded' which appear on Malaysian receipts.

repair_recommendations.change: Expand and reorder PRIORITY_TIERS to include rounding-aware totals and dataset-specific variants. New ordered tiers (highest first): [GRAND TOTAL], [TOTAL AFTER ROUNDING, TOTAL ROUNDED, ROUNDED TOTAL], [NET TOTAL, NETT TOTAL], [TOTAL RM, TOTAL: RM, TOTAL (RM), TOTAL INCLUSIVE OF GST, TOTAL INCL GST, TOTAL INCL. OF GST, TOTAL SALES INCL GST], [TOTAL AMOUNT, AMOUNT DUE, BALANCE DUE, TOTAL DUE], [TOTAL, AMOUNT, GRAND TOTAL (fallback)]. Document that when both 'Total Inclusive of GST' and a later 'TOTAL:' or 'Total After Rounding' appear, the later/post-rounding one wins.

Add explicit scan-all-matches logic: within the selected tier, collect ALL matching lines (not just the first), then pick the LAST one in document order (receipts place the final payable total near the bottom). This fixes cases where 'Total' appears multiple times.

Add a monetary-value sanity validator. After extraction, compute: candidate must be >= 0.9 * max(subtotal, any 'Total Inclusive' value) if those exist, and must be <= 1.5x that value. If the candidate fails (e.g., 702 vs 189.75 net total), fall back to the next tier or to 'largest plausible number within 3 lines of the top-priority keyword'.

Add robust fallback pipeline: if primary single-pass extraction returns None, invoke multi_pass_ocr (already drafted) and retry extract_total on the combined text. Only after all passes fail, set the field to Python None (not ''). Document explicitly: 'Set value to Python None; never empty string, never NaN, never the literal string None.'

Clarify date parsing: add a NOTE that this dataset is Malaysian receipts (DD/MM/YYYY). Code DATE_PATTERNS must try `%d/%m/%Y` BEFORE any `%m/%d/%Y`, and when both parse validly, prefer DD/MM. Add a validator: reject parsed dates where year not in 2010–2025 (adjust per task context) and re-try next pattern. Also, when day<=12 and month<=12 (ambiguous), log a warning and default to DD/MM.

Add a 'currency-anchor' heuristic: when searching for the total value, prefer numbers preceded by 'RM' or '$' on the keyword line or the following line; this helps on noisy OCR where other digits appear.

Document two-line fallback more precisely: if keyword-line has no decimal number, scan up to the next 2 non-empty lines; among all numeric tokens there, prefer tokens with a decimal point and currency prefix; take the last one.

Add OCR-digit confusion normalization step for amounts: common swaps (O→0, l/I→1, S→5, B→8) applied ONLY inside token positions that already look numeric (contain at least one digit and a decimal point).

In the batch pipeline example, explicitly show using `df.loc[i, 'total_amount'] = None` and verifying with `openpyxl.load_workbook(..., data_only=True)` that the cell value is Python None, not ''. Add a post-write check that iterates rows and asserts type(cell.value) is NoneType for failed extractions.

Add a short section 'Writing nullable string columns' describing: build list-of-dicts with None for missing, construct DataFrame with dtype=object, pass na_rep='' only when desired, and verify output cells are empty (not literal ''). Warn that `df.fillna('')` or using empty strings as sentinels will produce a cell with value '' which some verifiers treat differently from None.

Add an explicit 'Receipt-total selection algorithm' pseudo-code block near top of the skill summarizing: (1) OCR text → lines; (2) uppercase copy; (3) iterate tiers; (4) within tier collect candidates; (5) apply exclusions; (6) choose last candidate; (7) number regex + currency-anchor; (8) two-line fallback; (9) sanity validator; (10) multi-pass retry; (11) None on total failure. Make this the authoritative reference the implementing code must mirror.

Add warning examples section listing the specific failure modes seen in receipts like Brewery Tap ('Net Total' with rounding adj), Thai Delicious ('Grand Total' present but preceded by 'Total:' with same value — ensure neither is skipped, and total matches), and AEON/Daiso (which have 'Total Sales Incl GST' and 'Total After Adj Incl GST' — the latter wins).

root_causes.summary: When extraction fails, the pipeline writes an empty string in some cells rather than a true null, violating the task's 'value is set to null' requirement and breaking downstream equality checks.

The current skill prescribes keyword tiers + first/last tiebreak + two-line fallback, but offers no scoring that combines (a) keyword specificity, (b) proximity to rounding/payment anchors, (c) numeric agreement with Subtotal/Cash, (d) decimal-places plausibility.

skill_defects.defect: Prescribes 'take FIRST matching line scanning top-to-bottom (or last-match depending on receipt convention — test on sample)' without a deterministic rule, so the agent oscillated and ultimately defaulted to last-match, which failed on 074 and 077.

Lacks a 'final/bold TOTAL after rounding' rule: when a 'Rounding Adj' line is followed by a 'TOTAL' line, that trailing TOTAL is the receipt's definitive total and should outrank earlier 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' lines.
No numeric cross-check / majority-vote step among Subtotal, Total Rounded, Payment, Cash lines to catch OCR digit errors (e.g., 7↔1, 0↔O).

Null-handling guidance says 'set to Python None' but does not instruct explicit use of openpyxl None (not empty string) when appending rows, and does not warn that pandas may coerce None to NaN then to '' on Excel write for object columns.

Date extraction section lists patterns but gives no rule to prefer dates adjacent to the keyword 'Date'/'DATE:' and no rule to pick the FIRST plausible date (receipt header) over timestamps elsewhere.

Does not call out that strict string columns with occasional nulls must be written with openpyxl cell = None (not ''), and that pandas.to_excel with object dtype may still emit empty strings; no recipe for mixed string/None columns.

Not relevant to this run (not invoked), but offers no fallback-vision strategy for low-confidence Tesseract outputs; the skill bundle lacks a decision rule for when to escalate from Tesseract to vision LLM.

repair_recommendations.change: Replace the ambiguous 'first vs last' tiebreak with a deterministic ordered rule set: (1) within a tier, prefer a line that directly follows a 'Rounding Adj/Adjustment/Rounded' line; (2) otherwise prefer the LAST matching line whose extracted amount agrees (±0.02) with at least one other monetary anchor line (Subtotal, Cash, Payment, Total Rounded); (3) otherwise fall back to the LAST matching line; (4) only use the two-line next-line fallback if the matched line contains no decimal number at all.

Add an explicit 'majority-vote numeric sanity check' step: collect all decimal amounts from lines matching Subtotal/Total*/Payment/Cash (excluding tax/change/discount), and if a chosen candidate disagrees with ≥2 other anchor amounts that agree with each other, replace it with the majority value.

Add a 'final bold TOTAL after rounding' rule: if the text contains a 'Rounding Adj' line, any TOTAL/TOTAL: line that appears AFTER it in reading order outranks any TOTAL line before it, regardless of priority tier (except GRAND TOTAL which still wins).

Tighten date extraction: prefer the first date pattern on a line containing the token 'Date' (case-insensitive) or within 1 line of such a token; only fall back to global search otherwise. Document that DD/MM/YYYY is the default locale assumption and that a 4-digit year component disambiguates year position; add an explicit test that month ≤ 12 and swap day/month only when original month > 12.

Add explicit null-serialization guidance: when writing the output row, pass Python None (not '', not 'None', not float('nan')) to the Excel cell for failed fields. Show a snippet using openpyxl ws.append([fn, date_or_None, amount_or_None]) and warn against pandas object-column coercion to empty strings.

Document two OCR-robustness heuristics generalizable beyond this task: (a) when a single candidate's digit differs by exactly one position from several agreeing anchors (e.g., 702.00 vs 102.00×4), treat it as OCR noise and discard; (b) normalize common OCR currency confusions (RN→RM, O→0 inside numeric tokens) before keyword matching, but only inside tokens that already look numeric.

Add a short 'Mixed string + null columns' recipe: build rows as Python lists with None for missing values, write via openpyxl directly (not pandas) to guarantee empty cells rather than empty strings, and verify by reloading with openpyxl and asserting cell.value is None.

Add a 'fallback escalation' section describing a decision rule: if Tesseract-based total extraction returns None OR disagrees with ≥2 anchor amounts, re-attempt that single field via vision-LLM OCR for just that image, keeping cost bounded. Keep the recommendation generic (not tied to this dataset).

root_causes.summary: Last-match within a tier is not always correct when multiple same-tier totals coexist
root_causes.detail: For 077 the receipt has 'Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26' earlier and a bold 'TOTAL: 23.25' as the final line. Guidance says GRAND/final total — using LAST tier-4 match actually picks 23.25 (correct), but current script picked 23.26, suggesting candidate ordering or an early-return on a non-last candidate. For 074 the generic 'Total' tier captured 'Total Amt Rounded' producing 702 (OCR corruption), meaning tier-4 fell through past the specific 'Total incl. of GST' line.

root_causes.summary: GST/tax-summary cutoff and exclusion lists are too aggressive or too loose
root_causes.detail: For 078 ('Grand Total : 92.80'/'Total : 92.80') the pipeline returned null. Likely the summary cutoff (SUMMARY_HEADER_RE) truncated lines before the keyword, or an exclusion pattern (e.g. matching 'Total' adjacent to tax tokens) wrongly skipped the valid line.

root_causes.summary: Number regex rejects integer-only amounts and comma-decimal variants
root_causes.detail: OCR commonly drops the decimal point on receipts (e.g., '10.00' → '1000', '20,00' instead of '20.00'). Current NUM_RE requires a decimal in several branches, so lines where OCR lost the dot yield None and the extractor falls back incorrectly (contributing to 052/074-type misses in similar runs).

root_causes.summary: Single preprocessing/PSM path with no cross-check for ambiguous digits/dates
root_causes.detail: Only one preprocessing variant (grayscale+autocontrast) and one PSM (6) are used. For 034 this yields a plausible but wrong month digit. No multi-pass voting or consistency check between date tokens elsewhere on the receipt (e.g., 'Date: 09/03/2018' vs 'Time' header).

root_causes.summary: Date parsing does not disambiguate DD/MM vs MM/DD using surrounding evidence
root_causes.detail: The DATE_PATTERNS list orders DMY before MDY heuristically but accepts whichever first matches. For receipts with ambiguous slashed dates, no sanity check uses year/month ordering clues or repeats of the date elsewhere on the receipt.

skill_defects.defect: Rule for 'last matching line within a tier' is stated but implementation guidance is ambiguous about whether to prefer the FINAL printed total or the FIRST tier-match. Skill should explicitly state: within the highest-priority non-empty tier, take the LAST non-excluded line whose numeric value parses with a decimal; if the final printed line is a bold/standalone 'TOTAL' it must win over earlier 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' lines.

Number regex and normalization only handle `1,234.56` thousands format and `d+\.d{1,2}`. It does not handle: (a) OCR-dropped decimals ('1000' meaning 10.00) with safe heuristics, (b) European comma-decimal ('20,00'), (c) stray spaces inside numbers ('85. 54', '88 .17'). Needs a documented secondary normalization step with explicit safety rules (only apply integer-as-cents when the keyword line clearly has a monetary token like 'RM' and no decimal number anywhere else on the line).

Summary/exclusion rules are not scoped. The GST/TAX SUMMARY cutoff can swallow the final 'TOTAL' line when the summary header appears above it, and the exclusion list can match 'TOTAL' adjacent to tokens like 'GST' in the SAME phrase (e.g., 'Total RM Including GST'). Skill must document positive carve-outs: never exclude a line whose keyword is in the top-priority tier even if it also mentions GST/TAX, and only apply the summary cutoff when the summary header appears AFTER the first explicit TOTAL/GRAND TOTAL line.

Only one preprocessing + PSM pass is used in the batch pipeline, even though the skill documents a multi-pass strategy. For fields that fail (null date or null total) the skill should mandate a documented fallback: rerun with (a) PSM 4, (b) PSM 11, (c) inverted/thresholded variant, and merge candidates per field with a tie-break rule (prefer values that appear multiple times across passes).

Date extraction does not implement cross-field consistency checks or a locale hint. For receipts with slashed dates the skill should state: (1) if year is unambiguous (4-digit), day/month pair must be validated (day≤31, month≤12); (2) prefer DMY for MYR/RM receipts (Malaysian), MDY for US-style; (3) if multiple candidate dates exist on the receipt (e.g., 'Date:' and footer 'Print Date:'), require them to agree, else pick the one near the 'Date' keyword.

The xlsx skill emphasizes formulas but does not call out the specific requirement for OCR-extraction tasks: write `total_amount` as a two-decimal STRING (object dtype), write failures as empty cell (None), and never let pandas infer floats. Cross-reference between image-ocr and xlsx is missing.

repair_recommendations.change: Rewrite the 'Critical Rules for Receipt Extraction' section with an explicit ordered algorithm: (1) scan lines; drop lines matching exclusion regex; (2) walk priority tiers top-to-bottom; within the first tier that has any candidate, iterate candidates from LAST to FIRST but SKIP candidates whose parsed numeric value is implausible (e.g., exactly matches a quantity line, is 10x/100x the other totals on the receipt, or appears inside a line also containing 'ITEMS'/'QTY'/'ROUNDING ADJ'); return the first plausible candidate. Add a worked example showing 077-style dual-total receipts and 074-style 'Total Amt Rounded' noise.

Expand number regex and normalization: accept `d{1,3}(?:[,.\s]d{3})*[,.]d{2}`, strip currency prefixes (RM, MYR, $), replace a lone comma-decimal with a dot, and tolerate a space before the decimal point ('85. 54'). Add a documented 'integer-as-cents' fallback that only triggers when (a) the matched keyword is in tier 1 or 2, (b) no decimal number exists anywhere on the line, and (c) the integer has 3–5 digits (e.g., 1000→10.00, 2300→23.00). Mark this as HEURISTIC and document when NOT to apply it.

Tighten summary/exclusion rules: never apply the GST/TAX SUMMARY cutoff to tier-1 keywords ('GRAND TOTAL', 'NET TOTAL', 'NETT TOTAL'); never exclude lines whose primary keyword is 'TOTAL RM', 'TOTAL AMOUNT', or 'GRAND TOTAL' even if they also mention 'GST' or 'INCL'. Make exclusions require the exclusion token to be the leading/dominant token on the line, not a modifier.

Mandate a per-field multi-pass fallback: if `extract_total` returns None or `extract_date` returns None on the first (PSM 6 + grayscale/autocontrast) pass, run two additional passes (PSM 4 and PSM 11, each with an upscaled 2x variant for images under 1500px). Aggregate candidates and pick the value that appears in ≥2 passes; if all three disagree, prefer the pass whose candidate line also carries a monetary token (RM/MYR/$).

Strengthen date handling: add a step that collects ALL date-like tokens on the receipt, validates each (day/month ranges, year in [1990, current+1]), and when multiple distinct dates exist chooses the one nearest a 'Date' or 'Invoice'/'Receipt' keyword. Document DMY preference for RM-denominated receipts and MDY otherwise. For slash dates where both orderings are valid, prefer DMY unless the first field > 12.

Add explicit cross-reference to the xlsx skill: 'When writing results, keep `total_amount` as an object-dtype string with exactly two decimals (`f"{v:.2f}"`); write Python None for extraction failures; never let pandas coerce the column to float. Sort rows lexicographically by filename before writing.'

Add a 'Common OCR-induced number corruptions' subsection documenting known failure modes seen on receipts (dropped decimal, '0'↔'O', '1'↔'l'↔'I', '5'↔'S', '8'↔'B', ragged thousands separators) and the mitigations: character-class substitutions only when the resulting token parses as a plausible monetary value and the line is a strong keyword line.

Add a short section 'Writing OCR extraction tables' covering: object dtype for monetary strings, None (not NaN or '') for failures, pre-formatting to two decimals before DataFrame construction, single sheet named exactly as required, lexicographic sort by filename, and no index column.

Add a Quality Self-Check item: 'For each receipt, verify the chosen total line also contains a currency hint (RM/MYR/$) OR appears as the final printed total line; if neither, re-run the fallback multi-pass before accepting the value.'

root_causes.description: Within a priority tier, the agent takes the LAST matching keyword line rather than cross-validating against candidate values that recur elsewhere on the receipt (SUBTOTAL, CASH, line-item totals). OCR noise on a late 'Total Amt Rounded' line can inject a bogus number (e.g. 702.00 vs true 102.00 on 074.jpg) that dominates.

The number regex accepts single-decimal fragments (e.g. '88.1') produced by OCR truncation and formats them as '88.10', masking that the digit was dropped. No preference is given to candidates with exactly two decimal places matching typical monetary formatting.
Dual OCR variants are run sequentially but the first-non-null result wins; the agent never compares candidate quality (tier, decimal precision, agreement across variants) across both passes.

Ambiguous DD/MM vs MM/DD dates are resolved by first-matching pattern order rather than by locale/context (receipts from Malaysia overwhelmingly use DD/MM/YYYY). '09/03/2018' on 034.jpg was parsed as 2018-08-09 instead of 2018-03-09.
Missing/failed extractions are written as empty string in the xlsx cell rather than a true null/blank, violating the task's 'value is set to null' contract (078.jpg total_amount).

Keyword priority tiering, exclusion-list handling, and two-line fallback are correctly described in the Skill but the Skill does not warn about the two highest-impact pitfalls above (OCR-truncated decimals, cross-variant disagreement, DD/MM default, null-vs-empty-cell).

skill_defects.defect: Receipt total-extraction guidance tells the agent to format `f"{v:.2f}"` on any matched decimal number, with no rule preferring candidates whose raw OCR text already has exactly two decimal digits. This silently promotes truncated OCR like '88.1' to '88.10'.

The 'critical rules' section recommends taking the FIRST match top-to-bottom OR last, 'depending on receipt convention — test on sample'. This hedging produced the wrong choice on 074.jpg where a later OCR-noised 'Total Amt Rounded' line was selected over an earlier clean 'Total incl. of GST'.
No guidance on cross-validating the chosen total against other numbers on the receipt (subtotal, cash tendered minus change, repeated amounts) to filter out OCR hallucinations.

Multi-pass OCR section does not define a merge/vote strategy: when default and preprocessed OCR disagree, the Skill does not say to prefer the candidate from the higher priority tier, or with two-decimal precision, or with agreement across variants.

Date extraction patterns list ISO-like `YYYY-MM-DD` first, then DD/MM/YYYY, then DMY-month-name. For Malaysian/receipt corpora the Skill should state DD/MM/YYYY is the default interpretation for ambiguous all-numeric dates and MM/DD only applies when the first field exceeds 12.

The 'Null on failure' bullet says to set the field to Python None, but gives no concrete pandas/openpyxl guidance; the resulting xlsx wrote an empty string for 078.jpg, which fails exact-equality scoring if the oracle expects a blank cell / NaN. Needs explicit instruction: write None via pandas with dtype=object and verify the written cell is empty (no inherited '' string) before saving.

Does not document the convention for 'missing value' when writing a mixed string/null column: nothing warns the agent that `df.loc[i,'col']=''` is NOT equivalent to `None`, and that openpyxl renders '' as a non-empty cell. For OCR/extraction tasks this is the dominant source of null-mismatch errors.

No guidance on preserving string formatting (e.g. '47.70' not float 47.7) when a column is written with pandas; the current wording about dtype=object is only in the image-ocr Skill, not cross-referenced from xlsx.

repair_recommendations.change: In the 'Total Amount Extraction' section, change NUM_RE to require exactly two decimal digits for monetary candidates (`\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})*\.\d{2}` or `\d+\.\d{2}`), and keep a secondary looser regex only as a fallback when no 2-decimal candidate exists in any tier. State explicitly: 'Never promote a 1-decimal OCR fragment like "88.1" to "88.10"; prefer another candidate with full two-decimal precision from the same or lower-priority tier, or from an alternative OCR variant.'

Replace the hedge 'first or last match depending on receipt convention' with a deterministic rule: within a priority tier, scan top-to-bottom and keep ALL candidates; pick the candidate value that (a) appears with exactly 2 decimal digits, (b) is corroborated by at least one other line on the receipt (subtotal, cash, rounded total, item total sum), and (c) is nearest in position to the matched keyword. Only fall back to 'last number on next line' when the keyword line itself has no number.

Add a 'Cross-variant reconciliation' subsection: run at least two OCR passes (default PSM and preprocessed PSM 6). For each pass, extract (tier, value, raw_decimal_digits). Prefer: lower tier index > exact 2-decimal raw text > agreement between passes > variant with higher mean OCR confidence. Document the ordering as a short pseudocode block generalizable beyond receipts.

Rewrite Date Extraction: for all-numeric three-part dates, state the default is DD/MM/YYYY unless the first component is >12 (then MM/DD/YYYY) or the first component is a 4-digit year (then YYYY-MM-DD). Add a worked example resolving '09/03/2018' → '2018-03-09'. Keep month-name patterns unchanged.

Strengthen the 'Null on failure' rule into a dedicated 'Writing nulls to tabular output' subsection: assign Python None (not '', not 'None', not NaN strings), set the destination column dtype to object before writing, and after saving reopen the xlsx with openpyxl to assert that failed cells are truly empty (`cell.value is None`). Reference the companion xlsx Skill.

Add a 'Pitfalls specific to receipt totals' bullet list covering: late OCR-noised 'Total Amt Rounded' lines, 'TOTAL' substring inside 'SUBTOTAL' (reinforce exclusion-first), currency letters attached to digits ('702.00A'), and OCR confusions 1↔7, 0↔O that commonly affect the leading digit of amounts; recommend sanity-check that the chosen total is consistent with item total sum when item lines are reliably extracted.

Add a short 'Writing missing values' section: distinguish None vs '' vs NaN; show the pandas idiom `df['col'] = df['col'].astype(object); df.loc[mask,'col'] = None`; and recommend post-write verification with openpyxl that cells meant to be null have `cell.value is None`. Make this generalize to any extraction-to-xlsx workflow.

Cross-reference the string-preservation rule for fixed-decimal monetary strings (e.g. '47.70'): dtype=object, format BEFORE writing, do not let pandas or openpyxl re-cast to float. Include a one-liner example.

In the Quality Self-Check, add explicit checks: (a) every non-null monetary string matches `^\d+(?:,\d{3})*\.\d{2}$`; (b) every non-null date matches `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` with month in 1..12 and day in 1..31; (c) all null fields are Python None in the DataFrame and empty cells in the xlsx; (d) chosen total was NOT taken from an exclusion-keyword line even after OCR noise rewrote part of the keyword.

root_causes: image-ocr skill lacks a concrete, prioritized total-extraction algorithm: original skill only teaches raw OCR and multi-pass combination but gives no rules for keyword priority tiers, exclusion keywords, two-line fallback, or number normalization that the task prompt explicitly requires

No guidance on cross-candidate consensus (e.g., when multiple total-like lines yield different numbers, prefer the value that also appears in subtotal/payment/change-complement) to defend against single-line OCR digit errors
No guidance on handling impossible dates (month>12, day>31) via digit-confusion correction (0↔6, 1↔7, 8↔3) or by swapping day/month

xlsx skill does not warn that numeric fields intended as fixed-decimal strings (e.g. '47.70') must be written with object dtype / explicit string formatting; risk of pandas coercing to float and losing trailing zero

No skill documents an end-to-end receipt-to-xlsx pipeline template with: directory iteration, per-image try/except → null, filename-sorted output, single-sheet 'results' schema, header row, and no-extra-columns guarantee
image-ocr skill does not recommend upscaling small images or variant preprocessing specifically tuned for faint thermal receipts; agent had to discover this ad hoc
No budget-awareness guidance: skills do not instruct the agent to lock in a working extraction pipeline early and avoid iterative per-image tuning that burns iterations

skill_defects.defect: Missing structured-field extraction section for receipts (totals, dates). The 'When to Use' bullet mentions receipts/forms but no code or rules are provided.
skill_defects.evidence: Original image-ocr skill contains only raw text extraction and multi-pass OCR; task prompt gives explicit keyword priority list and exclusion list that the skill does not encode.

skill_defects.defect: No normalization rules for monetary values (strip currency prefix like 'RM'/'$', strip comma thousands separators, format to exactly two decimals as string, null-on-failure semantics).
No date-parsing/reformatting guidance (ISO YYYY-MM-DD output, handling of DD/MM/YYYY vs MM/DD/YYYY, month-name formats, rejection of impossible dates, optional digit-confusion repair).
Multi-pass OCR section aggregates text but does not instruct how to use multiple passes for voting/consensus on structured fields, which is what defends against single-digit OCR errors like 1→7.
No two-line fallback pattern (keyword on one line, number on the next) despite the task prompt explicitly calling it out.
No preprocessing recommendation specifically for small/faded receipts (upscale 2x before OCR); agent discovered this manually mid-run.
No guidance for writing fixed-decimal string columns (e.g., currency as 'NN.NN' string). Users easily end up with floats and lose trailing zeros / '47.7' vs '47.70' mismatches.
No pattern for 'write a dataframe to a single named sheet with exact columns, no index, no extra sheets' — a very common evaluation shape.
No guidance on representing null cells cleanly (Python None vs empty string vs NaN) when writing with pandas/openpyxl, which affects exact-match verifiers.
No end-to-end batch pipeline template (iterate directory, filter by image extension, sort by filename, graceful per-file failure to null row, assemble dataframe).

repair_recommendations.scope: generalizes to any receipt/invoice OCR-to-structured task

Add preprocessing recipe for small/faded receipts: convert to grayscale, autocontrast, upscale 2x via LANCZOS when max(dim)<1500, then run PSM 6 as primary with PSM 4 and PSM 11 as fallbacks. Document that this materially helps thermal receipts.

Add a 'Batch Pipeline to Tabular Output' section with a reusable function: iterate sorted(os.listdir(dir)) filtered to image extensions, run extract per file inside try/except, record None for failed fields, build a pandas DataFrame with explicit column order, keep string columns as object dtype.

Add explicit 'Critical Rules' checklist for receipt extraction: exclusions-first, priority-order-matters, two-line-fallback, strip-currency-and-commas, format-as-two-decimal-string, null-not-NaN-not-'None', sort-by-filename-lexicographically. These rules capture failures observed in this run and generalize to similar tabular OCR tasks.

Add 'Writing fixed-decimal string columns' subsection: show that currency/amount columns intended to preserve trailing zeros must be stored as Python str via f"{v:.2f}" and the column dtype set to object before to_excel; warn against float coercion.

Add 'Exact-shape single-sheet output' pattern: with pd.ExcelWriter(path, engine='openpyxl') as w: df.to_excel(w, sheet_name='<name>', index=False); emphasize no extra sheets created, header written as row 1, columns in declared order.
Add 'Null cell semantics' note: for strict verifiers, write Python None (not np.nan, not 'None', not '') for missing values; show how to coerce pandas NaN to None before writing when needed.

Add a 'Budget discipline' note: once a pipeline passes on 2–3 sample images, run it over the full set once and accept remaining OCR errors as null rather than hand-tuning per-image exclusions; this prevents iteration-limit terminations like the one observed.

root_causes.description: Rounding/adjustment lines (e.g., 'Rounding Adj', 'Total After Rounding') produce a FINAL total that differs from the earlier 'Total Inclusive GST'. Current logic picks first/last match within a tier but doesn't recognize that a later 'TOTAL:' line (after rounding) supersedes an earlier 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' value.

Date parsing is ambiguous for DD/MM/YYYY vs MM/DD/YYYY. The skill lists '%d-%m-%Y' before '%m-%d-%Y' in some flows but the current pipeline accepted an MM/DD/YYYY interpretation for 034 (09/03/2018 → 2018-08-09 implies the parser swapped). Receipts in this dataset are Malaysian and almost universally DD/MM/YYYY; the parser must prefer DD/MM over MM/DD when day>12 is not disambiguating.

OCR digit confusions (1↔7, 0↔O, 8↔B) are not mitigated by cross-validating against subtotal + GST = total arithmetic when both are visible. 074 shows GST 30.45 + ExclGST 507.55 = 538.00, but extracted 702.00 is arithmetically impossible — no sanity check rejects this.

Fallback for two-line keyword/number splits (e.g., 'Grand Total' on one line, amount on next) uses only the immediate next non-empty line and stops on first exclusion. For receipts with multi-column aligned totals (078), the number may be several tokens away or on the same line but mis-tokenized; current regex may miss it.

skill_defects.defect: Priority tiers treat 'TOTAL' and 'NET TOTAL' / 'TOTAL AFTER ROUNDING' as equivalent within tier 4. No sub-rule prefers the LAST total-like line after a 'Rounding' or 'Adjustment' line as the final payable amount.
No arithmetic sanity check (subtotal + tax ≈ total, or cash − change ≈ total) to reject OCR-garbled totals and fall back to the next OCR variant or candidate.

Date extraction regex order and format precedence are not explicit about regional convention. Should default to DD/MM/YYYY for ambiguous slash-separated dates in receipt context, and only fall back to MM/DD/YYYY when day>12 forces it.

Multi-pass OCR voting picks by (tier, frequency) but does not break ties using arithmetic plausibility or 2-decimal-string presence; a correctly-formatted candidate (e.g., '92.80') should outrank a mis-OCR'd one.

Two-line fallback terminates on first exclusion keyword in the next line; should instead scan a small window (next 1-3 non-empty lines) skipping exclusion lines, since receipts sometimes interleave 'Rounding Adj' between keyword and amount.

repair_recommendations.change: Add a 'final-total preference' rule: after collecting all tier-matching candidate lines, if any candidate line follows a 'Rounding' / 'Adjustment' / 'Rounded' line within the same section, prefer that later candidate as the final total. Equivalently, when both 'Total Incl GST' and 'Total After Rounding'/'Total RM'/'TOTAL:' appear, prefer the one closer to the end of the receipt body (before summary/GST section).

Add an arithmetic sanity check: if subtotal and GST/tax amounts are extractable from the same receipt, verify |candidate_total − (subtotal + tax)| < 0.05 (allowing for rounding). Also verify cash − change ≈ total when both present. Reject candidates that fail by >1.00 and fall back to the next-best candidate across OCR variants.

Rewrite date extraction to try formats in strict priority: (1) ISO YYYY-MM-DD; (2) DD/MM/YYYY and DD-MM-YYYY (default for receipts); (3) DD MMM YYYY; (4) MM/DD/YYYY only as last resort and only if the DD/MM interpretation is invalid (month>12). Document this as the receipt-domain default in the skill.

Strengthen multi-pass voting: for each OCR variant, record candidate (tier, raw_value_string, numeric_value). Score candidates by (a) tier priority, (b) presence of 2-decimal format in the raw string, (c) arithmetic consistency with subtotal+tax if available, (d) frequency across variants. Pick highest score.

Extend two-line fallback to scan up to 3 non-empty subsequent lines, skipping (not aborting on) exclusion lines, and also look on the SAME line to the right of the keyword using column-aware splitting (e.g., split by 2+ spaces) before falling to next line.

Add a per-image guard: if the chosen total string is not formattable as f'{v:.2f}' or if numeric value is implausibly large (>5× sum of visible item prices when items are OCR-visible), downgrade the candidate and try next variant/candidate.

Add a 'post-rounding keyword tier' between tiers 1 and 2: specifically match 'TOTAL AFTER ROUNDING', 'ROUNDED TOTAL', 'TOTAL ROUNDED', 'TOTAL RM' (standalone final line) and prefer these over 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' when both appear.

root_causes.summary: OCR digit confusion (1↔7, 0↔O, etc.) not mitigated by multi-pass consensus or sanity checks against subtotal/item sums

When multiple TOTAL-family lines exist with the SAME priority tier (e.g., 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' and final 'TOTAL:' after rounding), the skill does not prefer the LAST occurrence, which is typically the final payable amount after rounding adjustment

Two-line fallback logic is too narrow: when the keyword line has no number and the immediately next non-empty line is an exclusion keyword (e.g., 'Change'), extraction aborts instead of scanning further down for the amount or looking at the preceding/adjacent column
Date extraction does not disambiguate DD/MM/YYYY vs MM/DD/YYYY using contextual hints (e.g., day>12) or cross-check against other date tokens on the receipt
No fallback OCR variant voting across preprocessing modes (upscale, invert, threshold) that could outvote a single-pass digit misread like '102'→'702'

skill_defects.defect: The current draft's extract_total algorithm takes the FIRST matching line within a tier scanning top-to-bottom; for receipts where multiple same-tier TOTAL lines appear (pre-rounding and post-rounding), the final printed total is almost always the LAST one. Documentation even notes this ambiguity but code picks first.

Two-line fallback only looks at the single next non-empty line and bails out on exclusion; it should scan a small window (next 1–3 lines) and also inspect the SAME line for right-column numeric values when keyword and amount are separated by whitespace runs that Tesseract may split into two lines.
Multi-pass OCR variants are described but results are concatenated rather than used for per-field majority voting across variants, so a single-pass digit error propagates.
Date extraction patterns do not include a disambiguation step (e.g., if first number >12, it must be the day → DMY) and don't cross-verify against other date-like tokens on the same receipt.
No sanity check comparing extracted total against item-line sums or subtotal keyword values when both are OCR-visible, which could catch gross digit misreads like 102→702.

repair_recommendations.change: In the total-extraction rules, change tier selection to: 'within a matched tier, prefer the LAST matching non-excluded line (bottom-most occurrence) because final printed totals after rounding adjustments appear below pre-rounding totals'. Keep tier priority order unchanged.

Expand two-line fallback: when the keyword line has no numeric match, scan up to the next 3 non-empty lines; skip exclusion lines but do not abort — continue to subsequent lines until a numeric or a new tier-boundary keyword is encountered.

Add a multi-variant voting helper: run OCR with ≥3 preprocessing variants (grayscale+autocontrast, 2× upscale, binarized threshold) and ≥2 PSM modes; for each variant extract a candidate total using the same rules; return the modal (majority) value, breaking ties by (a) higher-priority tier, (b) value closer to a detected SUBTOTAL+tax approximation if available.

Add a 'plausibility check' step: if extracted total has leading digits that could be OCR confusions (7↔1, 8↔3, 0↔O, 5↔S), and a SUBTOTAL/items-sum is available on the receipt with a value differing by exactly a leading-digit substitution, prefer the subtotal-consistent candidate.

Strengthen date rules: (1) add explicit DMY-vs-MDY disambiguation — if either the first or second number is >12, assign unambiguously; (2) when both ≤12, default to DMY for receipts (document that this is a regional heuristic typical for Malaysian/SG/MY receipts in the sample domain); (3) collect all date-like tokens and prefer the one appearing near keywords 'Date', 'INV', 'Receipt', 'Invoice'.

Document and codify the rounding-adjustment pattern explicitly: 'If the receipt shows both a pre-rounding total and a final TOTAL/Net Total line separated by a Rounding Adj line, always return the final (post-rounding) line's value.'

Normalize numeric strings before validation: strip currency prefixes (RM, $), strip stray letters attached to digits (e.g., '86.17C' → '86.17'), and reject candidates whose decimal portion is missing (e.g., bare integers) when the receipt otherwise contains two-decimal amounts in the same tier.

Add a self-check that logs (not blocks) when the chosen total equals a line also matching exclusion keywords on an adjacent line (e.g., CASH TENDERED or CHANGE), prompting a re-scan for a tighter match within the TOTAL tier.

Picked GST-inclusive subtotal line 'Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26' instead of final 'TOTAL: 23.25' after rounding adjustment.
Extraction returned empty string instead of null when extraction failed; also failed to find a value (Popular Book receipt has 'Total RM 21.00').

root_causes.description: Two-line keyword→amount fallback is too permissive: when the keyword line has a corrupt/garbled number, the code falls through to subsequent lines (e.g., 'Visa RM ...') and picks a payment amount instead of the real total.
root_causes.evidence: Trace in exchange e0046/e0047 shows candidate 'Total RM = B81?' with no valid decimal number, then fallback consumed next 'Visa RM =688.17' line. Fix drafted in current candidate restricts fallback to keyword lines with no digits.

root_causes.description: Priority tier ordering does not consistently prefer the final rounded 'TOTAL:' line over earlier 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' line when both match the generic TOTAL tier. The algorithm takes last candidate in document order, but on receipts where the final 'TOTAL:' line is on a separate visual line from the number, it may miss it and fall back to the inclusive-GST line.
root_causes.evidence: 077.jpg predicted 23.26 (inclusive-of-GST line) rather than 23.25 (final rounded TOTAL).

root_causes.description: Null handling writes empty string instead of Python None when extraction fails, violating task spec that failures must be null (empty cell).
root_causes.evidence: 078.jpg total_amount predicted as '' (empty string) rather than null.

root_causes.description: Date parser does not reliably prefer DD/MM/YYYY over MM/DD/YYYY for Malaysian receipts, leading to swapped month/day when both interpretations are valid calendar dates.
root_causes.evidence: 034.jpg date predicted 2018-08-09 instead of 2018-03-09 for a '09/03/2018' receipt.

root_causes.description: Grand Total / final TOTAL detection does not restrict search to the summary/footer region of the receipt, so earlier item-line 'Total' entries (e.g., per-item totals in itemized tables) can be matched.
root_causes.evidence: 074.jpg predicted 702.00; receipt has itemized 'Amount' column with values whose last two digits may OCR as 702, while true Grand Total is 92.80 at bottom.

skill_defects.defect: Total-extraction fallback rule (two-line split) is specified but lacks a guard requiring the keyword line to contain no digits before falling through. Current skill text says 'when the matched keyword line has no number, take the LAST number from the next non-empty line' — this is ambiguous and allowed matching corrupt-digit lines. Needs tightening to: 'only fall through to the next line when the keyword line contains zero digit characters, and skip fallback lines that themselves contain payment keywords (VISA, MASTERCARD, CASH, DEBIT, CARD, CHANGE).'

Priority tier for 'final rounded TOTAL' is not distinguished from 'Total (Inclusive of GST)'. The skill should instruct: when multiple TOTAL-tier matches exist, prefer the LAST occurrence that is NOT labeled 'Inclusive of GST', 'Incl GST', 'Including GST', 'Excl GST', 'Excluding GST', 'Sales', 'TakeOut Total', 'Rounded', 'Before Rounding' unless it is the only match; otherwise prefer lines labeled 'Total Rounded', 'TOTAL:', 'Grand Total', 'Net Total', 'Total After Rounding', 'Total RM' (standalone).

Null output rule is stated but the batch pipeline example does not demonstrate guaranteeing None (not empty string) in the final Excel. Needs explicit guidance: before writing, replace NaN/''/'None' with Python None, and verify via pandas isna check.

Date extraction does not encode the regional convention. For receipts likely in Malaysian/UK/EU format (presence of 'RM', 'GST', 'SST', or Malaysian addresses), DD/MM/YYYY must be tried BEFORE MM/DD/YYYY. Current DATE_PATTERNS ordering tries 'DD/MM/YYYY' before 'DD/MM/YY' but doesn't disambiguate against ambiguous MM/DD cases, and the ISO-first pattern can grab a non-date numeric sequence.

No guidance to restrict total-amount keyword search to the receipt's summary/footer region (below the last item-line divider or below a 'Subtotal'/'Total Items'/'Item Count' marker). This causes false positives on itemized tables with 'Total' column headers or per-item amount columns.

Number regex accepts bare integers (e.g., '20') which can match item quantities or page numbers. For total extraction, should strongly prefer numbers with explicit two-decimal places; integers should only be accepted if no decimal number exists on the keyword line or its RM-prefixed value is unambiguous.

No explicit instruction that for pandas->Excel export, string columns containing None must be written such that the cell is empty (not 'None', not NaN-as-text). Suggest adding guidance: use df.astype(object).where(df.notna(), None) prior to to_excel, or set na_rep=''.

repair_recommendations.change: Strengthen total-extraction rules: (1) explicitly state that two-line fallback is permitted ONLY when the keyword line contains no digit characters; (2) add payment-keyword exclusions to fallback target lines (VISA, MASTERCARD, DEBIT, CARD, CASH, CHANGE, PAYMENT, TENDERED); (3) prefer last matching candidate within the summary region but demote candidates whose line contains 'Inclusive of GST', 'Incl GST', 'Excluding GST', 'Excl GST', 'Sales', 'TakeOut', 'Before Rounding'; (4) when multiple TOTAL-tier candidates exist, prefer those labeled 'Total Rounded', 'Total After Rounding', 'Net Total', 'Grand Total', or final bare 'TOTAL:'; (5) restrict primary search to lines appearing after the first occurrence of a summary marker (Subtotal, Sub-Total, Item Count, Total Qty, GST, SST, Tax Summary) when such a marker exists.

Add a dedicated 'Final Total Selection Algorithm' pseudocode block that: locates summary_start index, iterates priority tiers, applies exclusion keywords, applies demotion keywords, and only then applies the strict two-line fallback.

Expand date-extraction guidance: for receipts with currency 'RM' or Malaysian/Singaporean/UK indicators, try DD/MM/YYYY and DD-MM-YYYY FIRST; only fall back to MM/DD/YYYY when the day value exceeds 12 under DD/MM interpretation. Add a disambiguation rule: if both interpretations yield valid dates and no regional hint is present, prefer DD/MM for receipts (common for the dataset) and document this bias explicitly.

Tighten number regex guidance: for total_amount, prefer the rightmost token matching r'(?<![\w.])\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})*\.\d{2}(?![\w\d])' on the keyword line; accept bare integers only when no decimal match exists on that line AND the integer is immediately preceded by 'RM', '$', or ':' with whitespace.

Mandate null-not-empty output: explicitly instruct that failed extractions set the field to Python None; show a correct example that uses df.where(df.notna(), None) and writes with na_rep=''; add a self-check item: 'Verify no cell contains the literal string None or empty-string sentinel.'

root_causes: image-ocr skill's priority tiers treat 'TOTAL' (generic) and specific labels like 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' at the same priority as the final 'TOTAL:' / 'Grand Total' line; when multiple candidates match the same tier, there is no rule to prefer the LAST / bottom-most occurrence or to prefer a bold/standalone 'TOTAL:' line over an inline 'Total (Inclusive ...)' line.

Multi-pass OCR voting across preprocessing variants picks a majority numeric value without weighting by (a) which variant actually matched a priority keyword and (b) priority tier of the match; this lets a non-total number (e.g., a line total or subtotal from a noisier variant) outvote the correct grand total.

Keyword regex requires exact whitespace between 'GRAND' and 'TOTAL' and between 'TOTAL' and 'RM'; OCR frequently emits 'GrandTotal', 'GrandTota.', or 'Total:' with punctuation/colon noise, so specific tiers silently fail and the engine falls back to generic 'TOTAL' which hits the wrong line.

Two-line fallback accepts the last number on the next non-empty line without validating that the number has a decimal part; this lets noisy tokens like '92:80', '20', or OCR-split integers be accepted as monetary totals.

Date extraction does not disambiguate DD/MM/YYYY vs MM/DD/YYYY using contextual signals (e.g., Malaysian receipts are DD/MM/YYYY, two-digit day > 12 forces DD-first); when both components are <=12 the earlier pattern in the list wins arbitrarily.

Picked the pre-rounding 'Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26' instead of the final 'TOTAL: 23.25' after Rounding Adj -0.01. Priority logic did not prefer the final post-rounding TOTAL line over an earlier Total (Inclusive) line.

Empty string written instead of null/empty cell when extraction failed. Receipt (Thai Delicious) has Grand Total 92.80 clearly present; failure to extract plus writing '' rather than None violates null-on-failure contract.

Date parsed with wrong day/month ordering. Receipt shows '09/03/2018' (DD/MM/YYYY → 2018-03-09) but was read as 2018-08-09, implying either OCR confusion of '3' vs '8' or incorrect format assumption on an ambiguous numeric date.

root_causes.description: Total-selection logic does not consistently prefer the final post-rounding/net total when multiple TOTAL-labeled lines exist (e.g., 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' followed by 'TOTAL:' after 'Rounding Adj'). Current priority tiers treat them equivalently and pick the first match.
Failure path for total extraction writes an empty string '' instead of Python None, producing an empty-string cell rather than a true null, which may fail strict equality to null in the verifier.

Date parser does not robustly disambiguate DD/MM/YYYY vs MM/DD/YYYY for Malaysian receipts and is susceptible to single-digit OCR confusions (3↔8, 0↔O, etc.) without a sanity check against other date tokens or expected locale (DD/MM/YYYY).

skill_defects.defect: Receipt extraction guidance in current candidate skill does not specify choosing the final/last matching total when multiple same-tier TOTAL lines appear, nor does it describe handling 'Rounding Adj' lines that produce a post-rounding final total distinct from an earlier 'Total (Inclusive of GST)'.

Null-on-failure contract is stated but no explicit code pattern enforces None (not '') when writing to Excel; the batch pipeline example should guarantee empty cells for failed fields rather than empty strings.

Date extraction section lacks a locale/priority rule for Malaysian/SG DD/MM/YYYY receipts and does not recommend a plausibility check (e.g., prefer DD/MM/YYYY unless day>12 forces interpretation; cross-check with multiple date tokens on the receipt header/footer).

Improve date extraction: assume DD/MM/YYYY by default for receipts unless the day token >12 (then MM/DD/YYYY), and cross-validate with any secondary date on the receipt (e.g., 'Print Date', 'Date'); add OCR digit-confusion repair pass (try swapping 3↔8, 0↔O, 1↔l) only when the parsed year is outside 1990–2100 or month/day invalid.

Document that number parsing must strip currency prefixes (RM, $) and thousands commas, then format via f'{v:.2f}'; and that the stored cell type must remain string with object dtype to preserve e.g. '20.00' rather than 20.0.

Add explicit section for OCR-style outputs: when a column must be a 2-decimal string with optional nulls, use object dtype, write None (not '') on failure, and verify by reloading the file and asserting cells are either strings matching r'^\d+\.\d{2}$' or truly empty.

Add a verification pattern: after writing stat_ocr.xlsx, reload with pandas, check column set == {filename,date,total_amount}, row order equals sorted(filename), and that empty cells are NaN/None rather than '' or 'None'.

Add a 'summary region' heuristic: locate the first line after items (e.g., where 'SUBTOTAL'/'SUB-TOTAL'/'ITEM COUNT'/'TOT QTY' appears) and restrict total-keyword matching to lines at/after that index. This reduces false matches on header lines like 'Qty Price Amount' and item rows.
